# Triage labels

The skills speak in terms of six triage states: the Pocock Suite's five, and
`needs-clarify`, which is specflow's own. This file maps those states to the
actual GitHub label strings used in **burythehammer/claude-code-plugins**.

| Label in the Pocock Suite | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `needs-triage`     | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |
| `needs-info`       | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| none, specflow's own | `needs-clarify`    | Accepted, waiting on clarify for tickets |
| `ready-for-agent`  | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |
| `ready-for-human`  | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |
| `wontfix`          | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |

Three category labels — `bug`, `enhancement` and `chore` — also map to same-name
GitHub labels. Category labels deliberately do not map to the canonical
`spec_type` enum: they are a different axis, not a projection of it. `chore`
covers maintenance that is neither a defect nor a feature — dead code removed, a
dependency bumped, a stale reference repointed. It is a local addition: the
Pocock Suite's own triage skill names only `bug` and `enhancement`, and these
docs are what tell it otherwise.

Wayfinder labels are used verbatim, colon included, which GitHub accepts:
`wayfinder:map` and `wayfinder:<type>` (types: `research`, `prototype`,
`grilling`, `task`). Operations: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md § Wayfinding
operations`.

Apply and remove labels as `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` describes.

**Labels must already exist.** GitHub rejects an unknown label name rather than
creating it on first use, so applying a label that was never provisioned fails
the whole edit. `/tfuk-specflow:config` creates the set when this repo is
configured, skipping any that already exist; `/tfuk-specflow:doctor` re-checks
completeness. Add a missing one with `gh label create <name> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins`.
Spell them exactly — `ready-for-agent`, not `ready_for_agent` or `Ready for
Agent`.

These are **triage labels, not status**. Status is also carried by labels here
(`status:ready` / `status:in-progress` / `status:in-review`, with `done` being
the issue closed), but that is a separate axis owned by specflow's lifecycle
skills — see `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md § Status`. The `status:` prefix is
what keeps the two apart in one label namespace; triage states never take it.

One consequence of that shared namespace: GitHub uses a single label set for
issues and pull requests, so every label above also appears in the PR label
picker. Which labels a PR may carry is a repo convention, not a triage question
— see `docs/agents/conventions.md`.
